verdict.rationale: Vercel's 'Redis on Vercel' docs describe connecting Redis databases through its Marketplace for caching and real-time data, with credentials and environment variables injected into the project. Vercel no longer runs its own store: Vercel KV is discontinued and existing stores were moved to Upstash Redis. Missing for 10: a first-party Vercel-operated Redis-compatible store, any evidence of job-queue use, latency details or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a Redis-compatible key-value store for low-latency caching and job queues

citations.quote: Vercel lets you connect external Redis databases through the Marketplace, allowing you to integrate high-performance caching and real-time data storage into your Vercel projects without managing Redis servers.
Have credentials and environment variables injected into your Vercel project.
